duck_check_tests:
# string-search family - contract pins measured against DuckDB 1.5.5 (2026-07-26).
# All values below were probed through the vectorized path (table columns);
# literal-fold agreed on every pair (0 divergences).

STRSEARCH_SCHEMA = {"s": "str", "n": "str"}
STRSEARCH_ROWS = [
    {"s": "abc", "n": "b"},        # simple hit -> 2
    {"s": "abc", "n": "z"},        # miss -> 0
    {"s": "abc", "n": ""},         # empty needle -> 1 / TRUE
    {"s": "", "n": "a"},           # empty haystack -> 0 / FALSE
    {"s": "", "n": ""},            # empty-in-empty -> 1 / TRUE
    {"s": "abc", "n": "abcd"},     # needle longer -> 0 / FALSE
    {"s": "abcabc", "n": "bc"},    # first occurrence -> 2
    {"s": "aaa", "n": "aa"},       # overlapping -> 1
    {"s": "abc", "n": "B"},        # case-sensitive -> 0
    {"s": "héllo", "n": "l"},           # CODEPOINT position -> 3 (bytes would be 4)
    {"s": "héllo", "n": "é"},      # -> 2
    {"s": "héllo", "n": "él"},     # multibyte needle -> 2
    {"s": "a\U0001F44Db", "n": "b"},         # emoji = 1 codepoint -> 3 (bytes would be 6)
    {"s": "\U0001F468‍\U0001F469‍\U0001F467", "n": "\U0001F467"},  # ZWJ -> 5, not 1
    {"s": "ééa", "n": "a"},        # -> 3
    {"s": "xabc", "n": "abc"},     # suffix hit -> 2
    {"s": "abc", "n": "abc"},      # exact -> 1
    {"s": "é", "n": "é"},         # NO normalization -> 0 / FALSE
    {"s": "é", "n": "́"},         # bare combining mark -> 2
    {"s": "abc", "n": None},       # NULL-strict every argument
    {"s": None, "n": "b"},
    {"s": None, "n": None},
    {"s": None, "n": ""},          # NULL haystack + empty needle is still NULL
]


def test_strsearch_positions():
    for fn_expr in ["instr(s, n)", "strpos(s, n)", "position(n IN s)"]:
        duck_check(
            f"SELECT {fn_expr} AS r FROM __THIS__",
            STRSEARCH_SCHEMA, STRSEARCH_ROWS,
        )


def test_strsearch_predicates():
    for fn in ["contains", "starts_with", "prefix", "ends_with", "suffix"]:
        duck_check(
            f"SELECT {fn}(s, n) AS r FROM __THIS__",
            STRSEARCH_SCHEMA, STRSEARCH_ROWS,
        )


def test_strsearch_length_family():
    duck_check(
        "SELECT length(s) AS cp, len(s) AS cp2, char_length(s) AS cp3,"
        " character_length(s) AS cp4, strlen(s) AS by, bit_length(s) AS bits"
        " FROM __THIS__",
        STRSEARCH_SCHEMA, STRSEARCH_ROWS,
    )


def test_strsearch_length_grapheme():
    # Separate: only implement if length_grapheme lands in scope (needs a
    # grapheme-segmentation table; ZWJ family -> 1, decomposed e-acute -> 1).
    duck_check(
        "SELECT length_grapheme(s) AS gr FROM __THIS__",
        STRSEARCH_SCHEMA, STRSEARCH_ROWS,
    )


def test_strsearch_in_operator_is_contains():
    # `n IN s` over VARCHAR columns is string-contains in DuckDB (NULL-strict);
    # the pure-literal form `'b' IN 'abc'` is a DuckDB PARSE error. Gate this
    # test on the frontend actually parsing string-IN (sqlparser may reject or
    # mis-parse it as an in-list) - verify before enabling.
    duck_check(
        "SELECT (n IN s) AS r, (n NOT IN s) AS q FROM __THIS__",
        STRSEARCH_SCHEMA, STRSEARCH_ROWS,
    )


def test_strsearch_three_valued_where():
    # NULL predicate rows must be dropped by WHERE, same as FALSE.
    duck_check(
        "SELECT s FROM __THIS__ WHERE contains(s, n)",
        STRSEARCH_SCHEMA, STRSEARCH_ROWS,
    )
    duck_check(
        "SELECT s FROM __THIS__ WHERE instr(s, n) > 1",
        STRSEARCH_SCHEMA, STRSEARCH_ROWS,
    )
lowering:
Recommend SIX new IR ops plus pure-frontend desugars for the aliases. The whole family is TOTAL over (str|NULL) args: no trap conditions, no runtime errors, and every function is NULL-strict in every argument (all combos measured), so validity = AND of input validities — the strict-NULL vectorized fast path applies with no three-valued special cases. Rust byte-wise semantics reproduced every measured pin including normalization/combining-mark edges (validated against the probe corpus):

  // all ops NULL-strict; out_valid = s_valid & n_valid
  fn str_find(s: &str, n: &str) -> i64 {            // instr / strpos / position
      match s.find(n) {                              // byte index; "" -> Some(0)
          Some(b) => 1 + s[..b].chars().count() as i64,   // 1-based CODEPOINT pos
          None => 0,
      }
  }
  fn str_contains(s: &str, n: &str) -> bool { s.contains(n) }   // "" -> true
  fn str_starts_with(s: &str, n: &str) -> bool { s.starts_with(n) }
  fn str_ends_with(s: &str, n: &str) -> bool { s.ends_with(n) }
  fn str_len_codepoints(s: &str) -> i64 { s.chars().count() as i64 }
  fn str_len_bytes(s: &str) -> i64 { s.len() as i64 }

Byte-prefix/suffix/substring tests are exact because DuckDB does byte-exact matching with NO normalization and NO case folding (measured), and UTF-8 guarantees byte-prefix == codepoint-prefix.

Frontend desugars (all proven exact by 0-divergence corpus runs):
  strpos(s,n), position(n IN s), "position"(s,n)  ->  StrFind(s,n)   [note "position" 2-arg order is (haystack, needle)]
  prefix(s,n)            -> StrStartsWith(s,n)
  suffix(s,n)            -> StrEndsWith(s,n)
  len/char_length/character_length(s) -> StrLenCodepoints(s)
  bit_length(s)          -> 8 * StrLenBytes(s)      [mul propagates NULL; no overflow — VARCHAR length bounded far below i64::MAX/8]
  n IN s (VARCHAR,VARCHAR) -> StrContains(s, n)     [args REVERSED; only if sqlparser parses string-IN — verify first]
  n NOT IN s             -> NOT StrContains(s, n)   [plain NOT: NULL stays NULL, measured]
  s ^@ n                 -> StrStartsWith(s, n)

Do NOT desugar contains -> StrFind > 0: it is exact under three-valued logic (NULL>0 is NULL, matching contains' NULL), but StrFind pays an extra codepoint count of the prefix; keep StrContains as its own op. Do NOT lower length_grapheme via desugar — it needs Unicode grapheme segmentation (unicode-segmentation crate); recommend leaving it unimplemented (clean unsupported-function error) unless the corpus demands it. octet_length must NOT be mapped to StrLenBytes: DuckDB rejects octet_length(VARCHAR) at bind time, so binding it would be a divergence — mirror the binder error.
surprises: Positions are 1-based CODEPOINT indices, not bytes and not graphemes: instr('a\U0001F44Db','b')=3 (bytes would say 6); instr(ZWJ-family,'\U0001F467')=5 (graphemes would say 1); instr('héllo','l')=3.
Empty needle matches EVERYTHING: instr(s,'')=1 and contains/starts_with/ends_with(s,'')=TRUE even when s itself is '' — but NULL haystack still wins: instr(NULL,'') is NULL.

contains('abc', NULL) with a bare NULL literal is a BINDER ERROR (ambiguous with contains(MAP,K) and contains(T[],T) overloads) while instr/strpos/position/starts_with/ends_with/prefix/suffix all accept bare NULL and return NULL. A typed NULL (NULL::VARCHAR or a NULL column) works fine in contains. The engine must not 'helpfully' bind string-contains for an untyped NULL.

`n IN s` where both sides are VARCHAR expressions is string-contains — contains(s,n), args reversed, NULL-strict, empty-needle TRUE — but the pure-literal form 'b' IN 'abc' is a DuckDB PARSE error. A syntax-level literal-vs-column divergence; sqlparser support must be verified separately before wiring this.

The 2-arg call form "position"(a,b) binds (haystack, needle) — identical to instr/strpos — even though the SQL-standard form position(n IN s) reads needle-first. position('b','abc')=0, position('abc','b')=2. Also the unquoted call position(a,b) does not even parse (POSITION is grammar-reserved).

length() counts CODEPOINTS, not graphemes: length(ZWJ family emoji)=5 while length_grapheme=1; decomposed 'é' has length 2, strlen 3, length_grapheme 1. strlen is UTF-8 bytes. bit_length is exactly 8*strlen. octet_length does NOT exist for VARCHAR (binder error; BLOB/BIT only).

Zero unicode intelligence anywhere: no normalization (precomposed é never matches decomposed e+́ in either direction), no case folding ('Straße' does not contain 'SS'), and a bare combining mark ́ is independently findable (instr('é','́')=2). Plain Rust byte search reproduces every pin.
No implicit numeric-to-VARCHAR casts for any family member: instr(123,'2'), length(123), contains(INTEGER,...) are all binder errors — DuckDB will not stringify numbers here.

The family is completely total: no per-row runtime error exists for any input; every function is NULL-strict in every argument (all NULL combos measured), so the strict-validity-mask fast path is exact.

strpos/instr/position are bit-identical (strpos is NOT PostgreSQL's (needle,haystack) order — DuckDB flips it to (haystack,needle)); prefix==starts_with and suffix==ends_with exactly; len/char_length/character_length==length exactly (19-pair corpus, 0 divergences).
Literal-fold vs vectorized: 0 divergences across all 8 two-arg functions x 19 pairs — this family is safe from the constant-fold trap.
PostgreSQL's ^@ starts-with operator exists in DuckDB and equals starts_with.
